append.fast_path: vector end != capacity: store the record pointer at end, advance end by 8

args: end pointer (rsi, carried from the append block)
pointer to the record-pointer slot (rdx, from rsp+0x38 which always holds rsp+0x90)
grow_path.contract: reallocating append: the record pointer is moved out of the caller slot (the slot is zeroed) into the grown storage
grow_path.post_check: the caller then reads the slot and, if nonzero, calls the +0x8 destructor on the object it points to; on the move path the slot is zero so this step is skipped

append.iteration_end: the loop status message pointer at rsp+0x88 is freed, then the loop advances by 0x20

arguments.arg3_rdx: rbx, saved at rsp+0x10; passed as the third argument to every chain handler
arguments.context_rsi: saved at rsp+0x8; context+0xa0 is the chain-head object
arguments.file_type_r8d: saved at rsp+0x4; compared against 1 for the retry arm; stored into every record at +0x10
arguments.out_records_rcx: r14, vector of 8-byte record pointers {begin +0, end +8, capacity +16}
arguments.out_status_rdi: r15, status struct {u32 code +0, u16 subcode +4, message pointer +8}, returned in rax

callee_contracts.0x4f95600: file-list vector destroy helper used by the exception cleanup (internals not pinned)
callee_contracts.0x52091d0: output-vector per-slot destroy step (internals not pinned)
callee_contracts.0x52092a0: output-vector destroy range step (internals not pinned)
callee_contracts.0x5209430: output-vector destroy range call (internals not pinned)
callee_contracts.0x520a990: vector reallocating append from a caller slot (move semantics)
callee_contracts.0x529f350: element predicate: bool plus u32 gate plus u64 log number

callers_census.method: full .text e8/e9 scan plus whole-file qword scan
callers_census.note: enclosing functions of the callers are census only and are not pinned here

chain_b.head: object at context+0xa0
chain_b.rule: same ten-comparison-plus-fallback shape as the entry chain, against the +0x128 identity field
chain_b.second_slot: rsp+0x68 is written by the chain-B handler and copied into the record at +0x18 (second 8 bytes); its content semantics are not pinned
chain_b.status_move: after the handler, the scratch status at rsp+0x90 is moved into the loop status at rsp+0x80 (u32, u16, pointer; scratch zeroed; the previous loop message pointer is freed)

chain_b_failure.rule: loop status byte nonzero after the chain-B move: if file type == 1, run the retry arm; otherwise copy the loop status into out (pointer moved) and tear down the file list

driver_call.fail_rule: driver status byte at rsp+0x80 nonzero: copy the driver status into out (pointer moved, not string-copied) and tear down the file list; the loop ends
driver_call.slot_zero_rule: driver status byte zero and slot value zero: free the driver status message pointer and advance to the next element; no record is appended

entry_chain_a.failure_rule: entry status byte at rsp+0x70 nonzero: copy the status into out and tear down the file list; the main loop never runs
entry_chain_a.handler_effects: writes the entry status at rsp+0x70 and fills the file-list vector at rsp+0xa0
entry_chain_a.head: object at context+0xa0
entry_chain_a.rule: the head object plus nine successive +0x48 links are compared; the first node whose +0xf0 value differs from the runtime singleton wins; if all ten compare equal, the next (+0x48) node's handler is called
entry_chain_a.singleton_address: 0x5778260 (runtime value read from memory, compared, not a constant)

file_list.count_rule: element count = (end minus begin) arithmetic-shifted right by 5, passed to the reserve helper
file_list.dispose_rule: per element, if pointer != element+0x10, operator delete[] is called with (pointer, capacity at +0x10 plus 1); then the array is freed with size capacity minus begin

filename_builders.note: the builder internals are not re-derived here; only the call sites and argument registers are pinned in this item
filename_builders.type1_shape: per PR #1926: directory + '/' + '%06llu.log' formatted with the log number

loop_end.final_status: the entry status at rsp+0x70 is copied into out with a string copy of the message via 0x542efe0, then the file list is torn down and the function returns out
loop_end.output_vector_destroy: the out-records vector elements are destroyed via the range step 0x52092a0 and the per-slot step 0x52091d0 (stepping 8 bytes), preceded by the range call 0x5209430; the helpers' internals are not pinned

predicate_call.gate_rule: the element is processed only when the predicate returns nonzero AND the u32 output is zero; otherwise the loop advances by 0x20
predicate_call.internals: not pinned; the predicate builds a scratch string from the empty rodata at 0x1e629b and calls 0x529eb60
predicate_call.outputs: u64 output is the log number passed to the replay driver; the u32 output's meaning beyond the zero gate is not pinned

layout.plus_24: 16 bytes from rsp+0x60: driver out-pointer slot value, then chain-B second output slot value

reserve_call.contract: if the vector's element capacity already covers the count, return immediately; otherwise allocate count*8 bytes, move the existing elements, and free the old storage

retry_arm.entry_condition: chain-B status byte nonzero and file type == 1
retry_arm.step_1_rebuild: filename rebuilt with the type-0 builder 0x529d060

step_2_chain_a_prime.fail_rule: retry status byte nonzero: free the retry status message pointer and the filename string, then copy the loop status into out and tear down the file list

step_3_chain_b_prime.status_move: same move as chain B: scratch rsp+0x90 into loop status rsp+0x80
step_3_chain_b_prime.success_rule: loop status byte zero: append the record (same append path as the main loop)

step_4_chain_a_double_prime.entry_condition: loop status byte still nonzero after chain B prime
step_4_chain_a_double_prime.fail_rule: chain-A-double-prime status byte != 1: free its message pointer and the filename string, then copy the loop status into out and tear down the file list
step_4_chain_a_double_prime.swallow_rule: chain-A-double-prime status byte == 1: zero the loop status, free its message pointer and the filename string, and advance to the next element (the failure is swallowed)

status_struct.copy_rule: the six header bytes are copied verbatim (a u16 store at +0 and a u32 store at +2); the message pointer is either string-copied via 0x542efe0 (entry and loop-end paths) or moved (driver-fail and chain-fail paths)

teardown.common_exit: free the entry status message pointer at rsp+0x78 if nonzero, dispose every file-list string element, free the file-list array, check the canary, return out
teardown.exception_cleanup_region: 0x520d31e..0x520d3a0: dispose the filename string object at rsp+0xc0 (address saved at rsp+0x20), free the status message pointers, destroy the file-list vector via 0x4f95600, check the canary, _Unwind_Resume
teardown.filename_dispose_observation: the filename string is disposed explicitly on the retry-fail and swallow paths; no filename-string dispose is observed on the loop-end exit path in the window (per-iteration disposal via builder reassignment is not pinned)
teardown.landing_pads: 0x520e0ce..0x520e12e (eight endbr64 stubs moving the exception object to rbx and jumping into the cleanup region)

tool_versions.objdump_invocation: objdump -d --start-address=<start> --stop-address=<end> work/hl-node-94.bin, run from the repository root with the relative binary path; objdump --dwarf=frames for the FDE block

window.canary: fs:0x28 at rsp+0xe8, checked before return, __stack_chk_fail on mismatch
